observation.visible_scene: A small square gray concrete tabletop fire pit filled with glossy blue glass gems sits on a slatted wooden table. Two or more pale yellow-and-blue flames rise from among the gems. To the left is a gold pineapple-shaped planter with green bamboo-like leaves; to the right background is a dark wicker chair against a gray wall. The scene is a continuous close-up of the burning pit.
visible_changes: The flames flicker continuously: their height, tilt, brightness and the number of distinct tongues vary frame to frame (e.g., two leaning tongues early, a single tall bright flame around t=1.0s, two tongues again near the end).
Bright highlights and reflections on the blue glass gems shift and pulse in response to the moving flames, while the gems themselves do not change position.
The framing drifts very slightly over the clip (the left planter shows marginally more foliage at the top, the pit shifts a little within the frame), consistent with a slow, subtle camera movement.
The flame configuration is already in flux at the first frame and still active at the last; no ignition or extinguishing is shown.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fuel source and how the fire was lit are not visible.
Whether the flames persist, grow, or die out after the excerpt ends is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and cause of the slight framing shift (handheld drift vs. deliberate pan/tilt) cannot be confirmed from the background.
Apparent changes in the number of flame tongues are flicker/merging of the same fire, not separate ignition events.
